\label{ch:ar-spies-and-suspects}
\hlchaptermodality{346}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say to spy, to disguise oneself, to suspect, to sneak in and to chase.}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تجسس} (tajassasa)}{تجسس (tajassasa)}]{\ar{تجسس} (tajassasa) — to spy}

\label{lesson:AR-C346-tajassasa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to approach, then the Arabic for to move away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تجسس}}
\textbf{\ar{تجسس}} — \emph{tajassasa} — \textquotedblleft{}to spy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تجسس} \ar{الرجل} \ar{على} \ar{جيرانه}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tajassasa ar-rajul ʿalā jīrānihi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The man spied on his neighbours.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتجسس}, \emph{yatajassas}.

A spy is \ar{جاسوس}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تجسس}} (\emph{tajassasa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-s-s} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to feel with the hand, to search out news\textquotedblright{}. It is Form V; a spy is \emph{jāsūs}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tajassasa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tajassasa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tajassasa ar-rajul ʿalā jīrānihi.} — The man spied on his neighbours.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to approach, then the Arabic for to move away, then say \emph{tajassasa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تجسس} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To spy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تنكر} (tanakkara)}{تنكر (tanakkara)}]{\ar{تنكر} (tanakkara) — to disguise oneself}

\label{lesson:AR-C346-tanakkara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to move away, then the Arabic for to spy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تنكر}}
\textbf{\ar{تنكر}} — \emph{tanakkara} — \textquotedblleft{}to disguise oneself\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تنكر} \ar{الأمير} \ar{في} \ar{ثياب} \ar{قديمة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tanakkara al-amīr fī thiyāb qadīma.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The prince disguised himself in old clothes.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتنكر}, \emph{yatanakkar}.

A fancy-dress party is \ar{حفلة} \ar{تنكرية}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تنكر}} (\emph{tanakkara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-k-r} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}not to know a thing\textquotedblright{}. It is Form V, \textquotedblleft{}to make oneself unknown\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tanakkara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tanakkara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tanakkara al-amīr fī thiyāb qadīma.} — The prince disguised himself in old clothes.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to move away, then the Arabic for to spy, then say \emph{tanakkara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تنكر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To disguise oneself\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اشتبه} (ishtabaha)}{اشتبه (ishtabaha)}]{\ar{اشتبه} (ishtabaha) — to suspect}

\label{lesson:AR-C346-ishtabaha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to spy, then the Arabic for to disguise oneself.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اشتبه}}
\textbf{\ar{اشتبه}} — \emph{ishtabaha} — \textquotedblleft{}to suspect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اشتبهت} \ar{الشرطة} \ar{في} \ar{رجل} \ar{طويل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ishtabahat ash-shurṭa fī rajul ṭawīl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police suspected a tall man.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يشتبه}, \emph{yashtabih}.

It takes \ar{في} or \ar{بـ}. A suspect is \ar{مشتبه} \ar{به}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اشتبه}} (\emph{ishtabaha}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-b-h} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to resemble\textquotedblright{}, the root of the taught \emph{mushābih}, similar. Form VIII is \textquotedblleft{}to be doubtful\textquotedblright{}, when things look alike: to suspect.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ishtabaha}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ishtabaha}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ishtabahat ash-shurṭa fī rajul ṭawīl.} — The police suspected a tall man.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to spy, then the Arabic for to disguise oneself, then say \emph{ishtabaha} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{اشتبه} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To suspect\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تسلل} (tasallala)}{تسلل (tasallala)}]{\ar{تسلل} (tasallala) — to sneak in, to slip in}

\label{lesson:AR-C346-tasallala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to disguise oneself, then the Arabic for to suspect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تسلل}}
\textbf{\ar{تسلل}} — \emph{tasallala} — \textquotedblleft{}to sneak in, to slip in\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تسلل} \ar{اللص} \ar{إلى} \ar{البيت} \ar{من} \ar{النافذة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tasallala al-liṣṣ ilā al-bayt min an-nāfidha.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief sneaked into the house through the window.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتسلل}, \emph{yatasallal}.

In football, \ar{تسلل} is offside.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تسلل}} (\emph{tasallala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-l-l} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to draw a thing out gently\textquotedblright{}, as a sword from its sheath. It is Form V, \textquotedblleft{}to slip away or in unseen\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasallala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasallala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasallala al-liṣṣ ilā al-bayt min an-nāfidha.} — The thief sneaked into the house through the window.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to disguise oneself, then the Arabic for to suspect, then say \emph{tasallala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تسلل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To sneak in, to slip in\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{طارد} (ṭārada)}{طارد (ṭārada)}]{\ar{طارد} (ṭārada) — to chase, to pursue}

\label{lesson:AR-C346-tarada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to suspect, then the Arabic for to sneak in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{طارد}}
\textbf{\ar{طارد}} — \emph{ṭārada} — \textquotedblleft{}to chase, to pursue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{طاردت} \ar{الشرطة} \ar{السيارة} \ar{في} \ar{الشوارع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṭāradat ash-shurṭa as-sayyāra fī ash-shawāriʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police chased the car through the streets.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يطارد}, \emph{yuṭārid}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{طارد}} (\emph{ṭārada}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṭ-r-d} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to drive away\textquotedblright{}. It is Form III, \textquotedblleft{}to drive at someone, to hunt him\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭārada}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭāradat ash-shurṭa as-sayyāra fī ash-shawāriʿ.} — The police chased the car through the streets.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to suspect, then the Arabic for to sneak in, then say \emph{ṭārada} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
